summary: gyomu-python-analysis provides comprehensive tooling for parsing, analyzing, and tracking Python source code structures. It extracts metadata from classes, functions, variables, and Pydantic models, manages project workspaces and configurations, and supports snapshot-based change analysis.
responsibilities: Analyze Python source code structures, metadata, and dependencies.
Manage project workspaces, configuration, and module discovery.
Generate and compare project snapshots to track code evolution.
Provide AST-based parsing utilities for statements, expressions, and symbols.

capabilities.name: Python Code Analysis
capabilities.description: Extract structural metadata, types, decorators, and definitions from Python code elements including classes, functions, variables, and Pydantic models.

capabilities.name: Project and Workspace Context
capabilities.description: Initialize workspaces, parse configuration files, discover package roots, and load and cache Python modules.

capabilities.name: Snapshot Management
capabilities.description: Create project snapshots, enumerate target files, track changes, and compute structural differences across versions.

capabilities.name: AST Inspection and Indexing
capabilities.description: Parse and inspect Abstract Syntax Trees to evaluate Python statements, expressions, and build symbol indices.

design_decisions: Separates low-level AST statement and expression evaluation from high-level Python code element analysis.
Employs workspace and project context abstractions to handle multi-package configurations and tool discovery.
Maintains persistent file metadata and module caching to optimize repetitive analysis passes.
Tracks structural project snapshots with explicit diffing capabilities to monitor source code evolution.
usage_guidance: Use the workspace and project context components to initialize project roots and discover configuration files before running analysis passes.
Leverage the core analyzers and AST utilities to inspect Python classes, functions, and expressions, or extract symbol context.
Utilize the snapshot module to enumerate target files, create project snapshots, and compute structural differences between source revisions.
